draft.title: Physical changes
card: In a physical change, no new substance forms. The particles stay the same, but the way they are arranged or spread out may change.
Melting, freezing, boiling, condensing and dissolving are physical changes. So are cutting, bending and crushing.
A physical change is usually easy to reverse. Water that freezes into ice can be melted back into water, and salt dissolved in water can be recovered by evaporating the water.
The substance has the same identity before and after. Ice, liquid water and steam are all water.
draft.remember: Physical change: same substance, new form or arrangement, usually easy to undo.

a.q: Which change is a physical change?
opts: Butter melting in a warm pan
Milk going sour in a hot car
An egg cooking in hot water
a.why: Melting only changes butter from solid to liquid, and no new substance forms. The other changes make new substances, so they are not physical changes.
a.clue: Which change leaves the same substance behind?

b.q: Tom stirs sugar into hot tea and the sugar disappears. Why is this a physical change?
opts: The sugar is still there and could be recovered
The sugar has turned into a new substance in the tea
The sugar has been destroyed by the heat
The change cannot be reversed once it has happened
b.why: The sugar has spread out through the water, but it is still sugar. Evaporating the water would leave the sugar behind. Disappearing from sight does not mean a new substance formed.
b.clue: Disappearing from sight is not the same as being gone.

a.best: Butter melting in a warm pan

b.best: The sugar is still there and could be recovered
